items.title: fix(benchmark): check the MockMed encounter type as its own field
items.body:
## The defect

`verify_encounter_saved` is the **arm-independent success criterion** for the
compiled-vs-agent MockMed benchmark. Both arms are judged by it, so the
*comparison* between arms is unbiased — but every **absolute** rate it has
produced is too high.

It matched the saved encounter row as one fuzzy candidate string,
`<type> — <note[:60]>`, at `min_ratio = 0.8`. One similarity ratio over that
concatenation is decided by whichever field contributes more characters, so a
long correct note outvotes a short wrong type.

Measured on a retained MockMed frame (E4 precondition run, episode 4 of 20):
the agent saved the correct note under encounter type `Consult` instead of the
requested `Triage`, and the check passed it.

```
expected : 'Triage — Follow-up in 2 weeks; BP recheck.'
actual   : 'Consult — Follow-up in 2 weeks; BP recheck.'
ratio    : 0.8471   >=  min_ratio 0.8   ->  MATCHED
```

Verifying the defect against the actual screenshot found a **second,
independent path** that the original write-up did not name, and it is the
dominant one. The row check's fallback candidate was the bare
`note_text[:BANNER_NOTE_CHARS]` — a candidate with **no type in it at all**.
rapidocr segments MockMed's banner into `Encounter saved -` plus its own note
line, and that note line satisfies the fallback outright. On the episode-4
frame:

| candidate | best line | ratio |
|---|---|---|
| `Encounter saved —` (banner) | `'Encountersaved-'` | 0.8750 |
| `Triage — <note>` (row) | `'Follow-upin2weeks;BPrecheck.'` | 0.8000 |
| `<note>` (row fallback) | `'Follow-upin2weeks;BPrecheck.'` | **0.9180** |
| — | `'·Consult—Follow-up in2weeks;BPrecheck.'` (the real row) | 0.7750 |

## Why not raise the threshold

**There is no threshold that works.** On that frame the false-positive
evidence (0.918) is *stronger* than the true evidence the check requires
(0.875 for the banner). Swept over all 61 retained trajectories:

| `min_ratio` | TP | FP | TN | FN |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0.78 – 0.86 | 27 | **2** | 32 | 0 |
| 0.88 – 0.98 | **0** | 0 | 34 | **27** |

Both false positives survive to 0.86; at 0.88 every true positive collapses
into a false negative. The threshold has no separating value.

Removing only the type-free fallback is also **not** sufficient: the row
candidate still scores 0.8000 on that frame, exactly at the threshold, off a
line that contains no type.

## The fix

Structural, not a threshold nudge — each field is judged on its own terms.

- The row line is parsed into its **type field** and its **note field**
  (split at the first dash-like character, plus a positional split per known
  type so a dropped separator still parses).
- The type field is **categorical**: it must name exactly one member of the
  application's enumeration `ENCOUNTER_TYPES = ("Triage", "Consult")`, and
  that member must be the requested type. A wrong `Consult` can no longer be
  absorbed by a right note body, at any note length.
- The note field is **free text** and keeps the **unchanged** `min_ratio`
  fuzzy tolerance. Nothing about free-text matching is tightened.
- Both fields must pass on the **same** parsed candidate.
- A row carrying this run's note under a *different* known type now sets a new
  `wrong_type_row` field and fails the run — reporting silent wrong-action, as
  the reliability standard in `AGENTS.md` §3 requires.

This converges `verify_encounter_saved` on the discipline
`verify_hybrid_final` **already uses** in this same package: that function
scores the type and the note as separate line-level evidence and reports
`wrong_type_row`, and its docstring already names this exact failure mode.
The MockMed benchmark's criterion was simply never brought along.

## Validation — both directions, all 61 trajectories

The regression set is the 61 retained E4 trajectories with screenshots: 40
carry an independent in-page **record-oracle** label (`window.state.encounters`
read via `page.evaluate` — bypasses rendering, OCR and fuzzy matching), and 21
are labelled from the rendered encounter list.

|  | TP | FP | TN | FN |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| before (`origin/main`) | 27 | **2** | 32 | 0 |
| after | 27 | **0** | 34 | 0 |

**Exactly two episodes change verdict, and both are the known-bad one** (the
same seed in both 7B passes). Every known-good episode still passes. There is
no false negative in either direction.

Margins on the 27 true positives, against a 0.8 floor:

| field | min | median | max |
|---|---|---|---|
| type | 1.0000 | 1.0000 | 1.0000 |
| note | 0.9000 | 0.9000 | 0.9000 |

And the free-text tolerance is provably unchanged: every one of the 27 true
positives already satisfied the `<type> — <note>` row candidate at 0.8974, so
dropping the type-free fallback costs no genuine success on this corpus.

## Corrected numbers, with denominators

Denominator **n = 20 episodes per model per oracle**, pre-registered before any
episode ran and never adjusted.

| model | oracle | before | after |
|---|---|---|---|
| Qwen2.5-VL-7B | screen (pre-registered pass) | 14/20 | **13/20** |
| Qwen2.5-VL-7B | screen (confirmatory pass) | 14/20 | **13/20** |
| Qwen2.5-VL-7B | in-page record | 13/20 | 13/20 (unchanged) |
| Qwen2.5-VL-3B | screen and record | 0/20 | 0/20 (unchanged) |

Episode 4 moved in **both** 7B passes. The corrected screen oracle now agrees
with the independent record oracle at 13/20 in both, which strengthens rather
than weakens the run's replication claim.

## Tests

Both directions at four note lengths (11 / 22 / 33 / 60 characters), spanning
the band where the old ratio crosses the threshold — 0.7317, 0.8254, 0.8706,
0.9209 against the expected `Triage` row form. The benchmark's own 32-character
note sits inside the missed band.

- `test_right_type_passes_at_every_note_length` — the **over-halt guard**. A
  check strict enough to trip on OCR noise would make a working system look
  broken, which is worse than the over-count it replaces.
- `test_wrong_type_fails_at_every_note_length` — the regression.
- `test_wrong_type_row_beside_right_row_fails`
- `test_bare_note_line_is_not_an_encounter_row` — the second defect path.
- `test_unlisted_requested_type_is_still_checked`

**Mutation-checked**: with the fix reverted (old row logic restored, result
fields kept so the failures are behavioural rather than `AttributeError`),
8 tests fail, including all four wrong-type note lengths. Restored, all pass.

## Scope

`verify_encounter_saved` has exactly one production caller,
`benchmark/run_benchmark.py` (the MockMed compiled-vs-agent benchmark).
The OpenEMR benchmark uses `verify_note_saved`, a different criterion with no
categorical field, and is **not** affected by this defect; it is unchanged
here. `verify_hybrid_final` was already correct and is unchanged.

`VerifyResult` gains `wrong_type_row` with a default, so existing rows in
`benchmark/results.json` still parse.

`normalize_text` is now exported from `openadapt_flow.vision` (it was already
public in `vision.ocr`).

items.title: Fix MFMA total FLOPS calculation
items.body:
## Motivation

Total FLOPS calculation was hard-coded for `workgroup_size = 256` and `workgroups = 128 * cus`. If those were changed, e.g. `workgroup_size = 128`, the result was wrong.

This PR does not change any benchmark results. `workgroup_size` and `workgroups` is unchanged.

## Technical Details

MFMA instructions operate on a per-wavefront basis rather than on a per-lane basis. We need to convert from total threads -> wavefronts.

Old formula:  `total_flops = workgroups * SIMDS_PER_CU * iters * mfma_ops[type][arch]`

Correct formula: `total_flops = (workgroups * workgroup_size // 64) * iters * mfma_ops[type][arch]`



This was working only when `workgroups = 128 * cus` and `workgroup_size = 256`.

Old formula:
`128 * cus * 4 * iters * mfma_ops[type][arch] =  512 * cus * iters * mfma_ops[type][arch]`

Correct formula:
`256 * 128 * cus / 64 * iters * mfma_ops[type][arch] = 512 * cus * iters * mfma_ops[type][arch]`



## Test Plan

* Leave `workgroups` and `workgroup_size` unchanged. Run benchmark and verify results do not change.
* Modify `workgroups` and `workgroup_size`. Run benchmark and verify results still make sense.

## Test Result

Works as expected.

items.title: Ensure GPU finishes draw calls before benchmark timing
items.body:
Hi,

 Thank you for considering my PR.


 ## Issue

 Benchmarks involving rendering return wrong results. The end time is measured once `map._render()` method is called but we do not ensure that the GPU call stack is empty. We need to make sure that the GPU has processed all the draw calls
 before measuring this timestamp.
 If we start chrome without hardware acceleration (with CLI parameters `--use-gl=swiftshader --disable-web-security`), we can notice that the browser remains unresponsive and laggy for a very long time, whereas the benchmark result is almost
 as good as if we get hardware acceleration.


 ## Proposed solution

 To make sure that the GPU has processed all its draw calls, we read a pixel at the end of the benchmark.
 Of course, the rendering benchmark results became significantly worse.


 ## Benchmarks

 If we consider this benchmark for example: http://localhost:9966/test/bench/versions/index.html?compare=#LayerSymbol (we render a map with symbol layers).

 **Before:**
 Google Chrome, Macbook Pro M4 Max: `0.413ms`
 Google Chrome, Macbook Pro M4 Max with swiftshaders (hardware acceleration disabled): `0.440ms`

 **After:**
 Google Chrome, Macbook Pro M4 Max: `2.57ms`
 Google Chrome, Macbook Pro M4 Max with swiftshaders (hardware acceleration disabled): `171ms`


 ## Misc

 No related issues.
 This stackoverflow post also advises using `gl.readPixels` for WebGL benchmarking: https://stackoverflow.com/questions/38710140/how-do-i-benchmark-a-webgl-shader

 This PR does not include any visual changes and does not require additional tests. The public API remains the same (we are not supposed to use the added methods in the public API so I prefixed them with `_`).

items.title: Phase 4: pool+gather readout — empirical 24% rel-L2 improvement
items.body:
## Summary

Phase 4 evidence-driven design choice. The Phase-4 readiness doc and the toy 2D experiment (8.23% rel-L2 with the previous classic-FNO + pool readout) suggested replacing global-average-pool with a spatial gather at the receiver position. **I tested it and the obvious hypothesis was wrong** — but the *combination* wins. Results below.

## A/B benchmark (`scripts/bench_fno_gather_vs_pool.py`)

24×24 Gaussian-bump phantom dataset (80 train + 20 test, identical UNO backbone width=32 modes=6 depth=2, identical optimiser, 80 epochs, real j-Wave forward sim, deterministic PRNG seeds):

| Readout | Median rel-L2 | p95 rel-L2 | vs POOL |
|---|---|---|---|
| POOL (current default) | 13.82% | 42.74% | baseline |
| GATHER alone | 37.42% | 102.59% | **regresses 171%** |
| **POOL+GATHER** | **10.52%** | **22.65%** | **improves 24% (median), 47% (p95)** |

CPU runtime ≈ 50 s end-to-end (35 s data gen, 16 s training all three models).

## Why GATHER alone fails

A single feature vector at the receiver voxel discards the noise-averaging that pool gives, while not adding much new information — the UNO's spectral conv already mixes globally so the feature at *any* location encodes a global summary. The lookup at the receiver voxel doesn't surface unique spatial information.

## Why POOL+GATHER wins

Pool keeps the robust global summary; gather gives the head a receiver-localised feature when the wavefield response actually depends on it. Concatenated, the head's input is `2 × width` features (32 + 32 = 64 here), training time +5%, params +2x in the head only.

## What lands

- `src/brain_fwi/surrogate/fno2d.py`: `CToTraceFNO2DGather` (gather-only) and `CToTraceFNO2DPoolGather` (the winner). Existing `CToTraceFNO` (pool-only) unchanged — backward compatible.
- `scripts/bench_fno_gather_vs_pool.py`: the benchmark, deterministic, CPU-runnable.

## Dependencies

- Stacked on **#29** (UNO API followup test fixes). The test failures on `main` from the recent UNO refactor are blocking clean CI for everything; #29 unsticks that.

## What this is *not*

The 10.5% absolute median is still way above the <1% gate. This benchmark is deliberately small (80 train, 80 epochs, 24×24 grid) for fast iteration. The next levers — once the readout choice is settled — are: more training data, larger backbone width, multi-receiver gather (currently single-receiver), and the spectral-loss term already in `surrogate.train.surrogate_loss`. None of those questions land cleanly without first knowing the readout architecture, which this PR settles.

## Test plan

- [x] Benchmark reproduces the table above
- [ ] CI passes (depends on #29 landing)
- [ ] Re-run on the larger toy_2d_fno.py dataset (500 samples × 200 epochs) for the design-doc's authoritative comparison

items.title: fix(nl): heteromorphemic ⟨tj⟩ is two segments, not a palatalized affricate
items.body:
> 🤖 Auto-generated by Claude Fable 5 (claude-fable-5) via Claude Code — NOT human-reviewed. Verify before acting.

## Summary

Dutch (`nl`) error-cluster diagnosis on WikiPron gold (bench-harness methodology: harness first, cluster by phenomenon, fix only what is rule-governed and citable). One real bug found and fixed, plus a closed loanword/placename exception set for the minority pronunciation this fix now generalizes away from. The rest of the residual gap to espeak is confirmed lexical or belongs to the in-progress `feat/grammatical-endings` mechanism, not this spec.

Adversarial review round 1 (APPROVE on the linguistics: full-corpus sweep, 318 changed words all `⟨tj⟩`, 317 better / 1 worse, `-ntje`/`-ltje`/`-rtje` all confirmed `[tj]` in gold, `tsj` untouched, `water` unchanged, merged suite green) flagged two follow-ups, both addressed in this revision: the other three `nl` scoreboard rows were not rescored, and the CI-sample claim was wrong (see "CI-sample correction" below — the wrong number in the earlier revision was actually a harness invocation bug, not a real regression).

## What was fixed

`⟨tj⟩` was pinned to a single coalesced segment (`tʲ`/`tʃ`). WikiPron gold shows this is wrong for the overwhelming majority of `⟨tj⟩` words: the productive diminutive suffix `-tje`/`-etje` attached after a stem-final plosive (katje, potje, witje) keeps the stem's coda `/t/` and the suffix's onset `/j/` distinct across the morpheme boundary, and word-initial `⟨tj-⟩` placenames (Tjalk, Tjonge) are `[tj]` too (Booij 1995, *The Phonology of Dutch*, ch. 2–3). Removing the digraph entry lets `⟨tj⟩` fall through to the existing plain `⟨t⟩`+`⟨j⟩` graphemes, which also fixed a second-order bug: the coalesced digraph was being counted as a single intervocalic consonant by the open-syllable-lengthening rule, wrongly lengthening the diminutive stem vowel (`witje` → *`[ʋiːtʲə]` instead of `[ʋɪtjə]`, since `tj` is phonemically two segments — a closed syllable, not one).

- `tje`-diminutive cluster (n=188): mean PER 0.2199 → 0.0713 (now in line with the `kje`/`pje`/`etje` diminutive allomorphs, 0.065–0.082).

## Closed exception set for tautomorphemic ⟨tj⟩ (this revision)

The general `[tj]` rule is a majority pattern, not universal: a small closed set of Malay/Indonesian loanwords (the `ketjap`/`tjap` "seal, brand" family) and Frisian-influenced placenames keep `⟨tj⟩` as the coalesced affricate `[tʃ]` because in these words it is **tautomorphemic** (one morpheme, one syllable onset), not a morpheme boundary. Per `AGENTS.md` §2 ("a closed irregular set → `word_exceptions`; a productive pattern → the rule layer"), pinned as `word_exceptions`, each entry's gold pronunciation taken directly from WikiPron:

| word | IPA | note |
|---|---|---|
| tjap | ˈtʃɑp | "seal, brand" (Malay loan) |
| tjappen | ˈtʃɑpən | verb, tjap-family |
| tjaffelen | ˈtʃɑfələn | tjap-family |
| tjanten | ˈtʃɑntən | tjap-family |
| tjetten | ˈtʃɛtən | tjap-family |
| tjaptjoi | ˈtʃɑptʃɔi | Indonesian-Dutch dish |
| tjauwmin | ˈtʃɑumɪn | Indonesian-Dutch dish |
| tjokvol | ˈtʃɔkfɔl | "chock-full" (loan blend) |
| matjok | ˈmaːtʃɔk | loan |
| nestje | ˈnɛstʃə | (⟨st⟩+⟨j⟩ coalescence, not diminutive here) |
| Tietjerk | ˈtitʃɛrk | Frisian placename |
| Tjalhuizum | ˈtʃɑlɦœyzʏm | Frisian placename |
| Tjerkgaast | ˈtʃɛrkɣaːst | Frisian placename |
| Tjerkwerd | ˈtʃɛrkʋərt | Frisian placename |

**Deliberately excluded** (adversarial check against the candidate list, which named 16 including `tjalk` and `ketjap` — both were dropped after checking gold):
- `ketjap` — WikiPron records **both** `[tj]` and `[tʃ]` as attested pronunciation variants under the identical key. Multi-reference scoring already credits either, so the general rule already scores this word correctly; adding an override would be a no-op at best.
- `tjalk` — genuinely ambiguous at the same lowercased key: the placename **Tjalk** (Friesland) is gold `[tj]`, the common noun **tjalk** (a sailing barge) is gold `[tʃ]`. Word-exception lookup is case-insensitive (`_override_for` lowercases before matching), so a single override cannot satisfy both senses without regressing one of them. Left on the general (majority-consistent, placename-correct) `[tj]` rule.

Two new adversarial tests pin 3 of the 14 exceptions plus the two deliberately-excluded ambiguous cases (`tests/test_germanic.py::TestDutchBeatEspeakWave::test_tautomorphemic_tj_loanwords_pinned_as_exceptions`, `::test_ambiguous_tjalk_and_ketjap_left_on_general_rule`), verified failing before the exceptions were added and passing after.

## Cluster breakdown (worst-200 words, full-dataset random sample; not the alphabetically-biased default `error_analysis.py` slice)

| Cluster | n | Rule-governed? | Action |
|---|---|---|---|
| Heteromorphemic `⟨tj⟩` (diminutive -tje, `Tj-` placenames) | 188 | Yes — Booij 1995 ch. 2–3 | **Fixed this PR** |
| Tautomorphemic `⟨tj⟩` loanwords/placenames | 14 | Yes — closed set, `word_exceptions` | **Fixed this PR** |
| `kje`/`pje`/`etje` diminutive allomorphs | 113 | N/A — already correct | No action, confirmed as guard |
| Loanword `⟨ch⟩` = [ʃ] (French/English: cheque, quiche, douche, niche, broche…) | ~20 in worst-200 | Lexically conditioned (loan-origin identification needed, not a general Dutch grapheme) | Lexical — record for lexicon, not a grapheme hack |
| Acronyms / letter-name spellings (A, CAO, CDA, AVG, VOC…) | ~40 in worst-200 | Lexical (letter names) | Lexical, out of scope |
| Loanword `⟨ng⟩+V` retaining [ɡ] (conga, tango, mango, tanga…) | ~15 in worst-200 | Lexically conditioned (native `⟨ng⟩` is genuinely [ŋ] with no [ɡ]; can't generalize without breaking native words) | Lexical — record for lexicon |
| Compound-final `ɛ`→wrongly-reduced-to-`ə` (koffiemelk, brandmerk, aanzegger, omwenteling, dierentemmer…) | thousands of confusion-pair instances, open class | Rule-governed (Booij 1995 ch. 5: non-head compound members carry secondary stress and resist unstressed-e reduction) but requires general **compound-boundary/stress-assignment** logic, not a closed list — a prior wave already pinned a small closed set (`berg`/`veld`/`kerk`/`brecht`). Extending this needs proper compound segmentation. | **Recorded for the `feat/grammatical-endings` mechanism being built in parallel** — this is exactly the class of thing that mechanism should own; not hacked here as more pinned morpheme chunks |
| Foreign/loanword phonology generally (China, chino, macho, beagle, bingo, foyer, revers…) | large share of worst-200 | Lexical (loanword-specific phonology, not derivable from Dutch orthography rules) | Lexical, out of scope |

## Numbers — all four registered nl datasets

| dataset | provenance | before | after | Δ |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| wikipron | crowd-scraped (human, Wiktionary) | 0.1262 | **0.1251** | −0.0011 |
| ipadict | machine-generated | 0.1616 | **0.1605** | −0.0011 |
| vox_communis | epitran-derived | 0.2732 | **0.2722** | −0.0010 |
| ipa_childes | **espeak-derived** | 0.2520 | **0.2586** | **+0.0066 (worse)** |

**Honest framing of the ipa_childes regression:** `ipa_childes` gold for `nl` is *espeak's own output*, reused as a reference (see `docs/benchmarks.md`, "espeak-derived" tier — measures agreement with a competitor, not correctness). eSpeak coalesces `⟨tj⟩` the same wrong way our spec used to. Diverging from espeak's coalesced-`⟨tj⟩` analysis to follow the actual human-annotated WikiPron gold and Booij (1995) necessarily *lowers* agreement with espeak's output on this dataset — that is expected and correct, not a quality regression. The three datasets with real (non-espeak-derived) gold all improved.

espeak comparison (wikipron, the only nl row with a registered espeak comparison): 0.1251 vs espeak 0.1099.

## CI-sample correction (round 2)

The previous revision's claim that `benchmarks/results_ci_sample.json` was unchanged was itself wrong, but not for the reason initially suspected. Root cause: running `scripts/benchmark.py --ci-sample` as a bare script (not `-c`) puts the script's own directory (`scripts/`) at `sys.path[0]`, not the repo root, so `from orthography2ipa import G2P` silently resolved to a **stale pip-installed `orthography2ipa==7.56.0a2`** in the shared venv instead of this checkout — exactly the gotcha the CI workflow comment warns about ("Measure the checkout (`PYTHONPATH=$PWD`), not any installed package"). Re-ran with `PYTHONPATH=$PWD` as the CI does; all four nl rows in `results_ci_sample.json` (the fixed `--limit 1000` uniform sample, `n=828` for wikipron) are confirmed **unchanged** by this PR's fixes — the alphabetically-first `A*`-heavy CI sample slice contains no affected `⟨tj⟩` words. File left byte-identical, not committed.

## Method

- `scripts/benchmark.py --dataset wikipron --lang nl` for the aggregate.
- `scripts/error_analysis.py --json` was checked but its default `--limit 300` head-of-file sample is alphabetically biased (WikiPron nl gold is sorted) — dominated by A-initial acronyms/proper nouns, not representative. Built a standalone full-dataset scorer (scratch, not committed) reusing `benchmark.align`/`normalize`/`levenshtein` to get an unbiased worst-200 sample and per-cluster regex stats before touching any rule.
- Adversarial tests, all verified failing pre-fix / passing post-fix:
  - `test_heteromorphemic_tj_stays_two_segments`, `test_tj_does_not_trigger_open_syllable_lengthening` (the general rule)
  - `test_tautomorphemic_tj_loanwords_pinned_as_exceptions`, `test_ambiguous_tjalk_and_ketjap_left_on_general_rule` (the closed exception set)
- Full suite: 197000 passed, 5 skipped, 134 xfailed, 0 failed — no regressions.
- All four nl datasets (wikipron, ipadict, vox_communis, ipa_childes) rescored with `PYTHONPATH=$PWD` against the current checkout.

## Files changed

- `orthography2ipa/data/nl.json` — removed the `tj` digraph grapheme entry; added `word_exceptions` for the 14-word closed tautomorphemic-`⟨tj⟩` set; documented both + citations in the spec's `notes`.
- `tests/test_germanic.py` — four adversarial regression tests in `TestDutchBeatEspeakWave`.
- `benchmarks/results.json`, `docs/scoreboard.md`, `benchmarks/comparison.json`, `docs/comparison.md` — surgical row updates for all four `nl` rows (wikipron, ipadict, vox_communis, ipa_childes), including the honest `ipa_childes` regression.
- `benchmarks/results_ci_sample.json` — confirmed byte-identical after regeneration with the CI's own `PYTHONPATH=$PWD` invocation; not committed (no actual diff).

## Test plan

- [x] All four new/updated adversarial tests fail before their respective fix, pass after
- [x] Full test suite green (197000 passed, 0 failed)
- [x] `scripts/benchmark.py --dataset <ds> --lang nl` re-run after all fixes for all four datasets, table above
- [x] `results_ci_sample.json` regenerated with `PYTHONPATH=$PWD` (the CI's own invocation) and confirmed unchanged by direct diff

items.title: fix(evolution): version_label + version_filter are content-scoping, not tier-gated (closes #17, #18)
items.body:
Closes #17 and #18. Both bugs were variants of the same mistake: treating \`version_label\` (caller-supplied opaque content) like an evolution-scoring signal that should be hidden when \`evolution_tier == \"off\"\`. It isn't.

Reported by @dx-poc folks; their two-workaround stack (\`EnterpriseDB/dx-poc#126\`) drops down to one once this lands.

## #17: \`ChunkResult.version_label\` was always None at tier=off

\`retrieval.py:query()\` previously projected:

\`\`\`python
version_label=(row.get(\"version_label\") if evo_on else None),
\`\`\`

Every SQL builder fetches \`d.version_label\` (the data IS in the row dict), but the projection discarded it whenever \`tier=\"off\"\`. dx-poc carried a workaround that re-joined \`documents\` per chunk in their proxy layer — extra round trip per query.

**Fix:** treat \`version_label\` like \`metadata\` (PRG-1 line above it) — caller-supplied opaque content, surface regardless of tier. The other state fields (\`retracted\`, \`effective_from\`, \`effective_to\`, \`superseded_by_id\`) stay tier-gated because they're real scoring signals.

## #18: \`version_filter\` silently no-op'd at tier=off

\`evolution_where_clauses()\` had \`if tier == \"off\": return [], {}\` at the top, which short-circuited the whole clause list — including the \`version_filter\` clause emitted at the bottom. So \`rag.ask(version_filter=\"3.12\")\` at the default tier returned chunks from every version with no error or warning.

**Fix:** emit the \`version_filter\` clause BEFORE the tier-off short-circuit. The tier-off path now returns \`[version_label clause]\` (not \`[]\`) when \`version_filter\` is set, while still skipping the scoring-gated clauses (\`retracted\`, supersession, \`as_of\`).

## The conceptual cut

| Behavior | Tier-dependent? | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Temporal boost, supersession penalty, retraction multiplier | **Yes** (scoring) | Re-shapes ranking; only meaningful when evolution is on |
| \`retracted_behavior=hide\` filter | **Yes** (stateful filter) | Pairs with retraction scoring |
| \`supersession_behavior=hide\` filter | **Yes** (stateful filter) | Pairs with supersession scoring |
| \`as_of\` temporal window | **Yes** (relies on \`effective_from\`/\`effective_to\`) | Time-travel is an evolution-specific operation |
| **\`version_filter\` content scope** | **No** (this PR) | \"Restrict to docs with version_label='X'\" is a WHERE clause, not a scoring decision |
| **\`ChunkResult.version_label\` projection** | **No** (this PR) | User's own opaque data, written at ingest. Same shape as \`metadata\` |

dx-poc described the distinction cleanly in #18: \"Evolution scoring vs evolution scoping are conceptually distinct; the current design ties them together such that callers who don't want the re-shaping behavior also can't use the scoping behavior.\" This PR is that fix.

## Tests (11 new, 199 total)

- \`version_filter\` emits at tier=off (the core fix for #18)
- \`version_filter\` emits at tier=structural (no regression)
- No \`version_filter\` + tier=off → still empty (preserves intent)
- Scoring filters STILL tier-gated at tier=off (\`retracted\`, supersession)
- \`version_filter\` at tier=off doesn't drag in scoring filters
- \`doc_alias\` parameter threads through correctly (alias-agnostic)
- \`evolution_aware=False\` per-call override behaves the same
- **Source-level pin**: every SQL builder SELECTs \`d.version_label\` (#17 regression guard)
- **Source-level pin**: \`query()\` projects \`version_label\` directly, not gated by \`evo_on\` (#17 regression guard — fails loudly if a future refactor regresses)

## Downstream impact

EnterpriseDB/dx-poc carries a 3-layer workaround. Two layers go away with this PR:
- The proxy-layer SQL join to re-fetch \`documents.version_label\` per chunk (#17)
- The proxy-layer post-filter loop \`if chunk.version_label != version_filter: continue\` (#18 — pg-raggraph now does the SQL filter correctly)

The third layer (defense-in-depth) stays.

## Verification

- [x] \`uv run pytest tests/unit/\` — **199/199 pass** (188 → +11)
- [x] \`uv run pre-commit run --all-files\` — both ruff hooks pass

## Backward compatibility

\`version_filter=None\` at tier=off was \`return [], {}\` (no clauses) → still \`return [], {}\` (no clauses). \`version_filter=\"X\"\` at tier=off was a silent no-op → now applies the WHERE clause. The semantic change is **strict tightening**: callers who passed \`version_filter\` were getting wrong results; now they get correct results. No existing tests or benchmarks break.

items.title: Force Referee solver path for game and audit hint flows and add solverPath debug/reporting
items.body:
### Motivation
- Ensure both interactive Hint/Solve and the audit “new hint” flows explicitly exercise the Referee solver path instead of silently falling back to legacy routing. 
- Make solver routing observable in logs and audit output so audit results cannot accidentally benchmark the wrong engine. 
- Keep solver logic and hint-blind behavior unchanged while making the chosen solver explicit and debuggable.

### Description
- Updated `APP.Solver.solveLevel(...)` to record and return `solverPath: 'legacy' | 'referee'` and to set that field explicitly in both legacy and Referee branches (including error/abort early-returns). 
- Added concise debug logging inside `solveLevel` that prints `purpose`, `levelId`, `solverPath`, whether `allowReferee` was requested, and the `escalationTierUsed`. 
- Forced Referee usage by passing `allowReferee: true` from the runtime flow in `runGameSolver(...)`, and added a short `console.info` showing the returned `solverPath` for interactive attempts. 
- Forced Referee usage in the audit/new-hint flow by adding `allowReferee: true` to every staged `solveLevel(...)` call (A/B/C attempts and the Gemini fallback), storing `solverPath` on attempt records and the per-level audit result, and exposing `solverPath` in the rendered audit lines (e.g., `solver=referee`). 
- Preserved existing UI messages, hint-blind transformations, and fallback-to-legacy behavior when Referee is inconclusive; no solver heuristics or level formats were changed.

### Testing
- Ran a JS syntax check of the concatenated inline scripts using `node --check` against the built script bundle and it passed. (succeeded)
- Served the app locally with `python -m http.server` and exercised the page via an automated Playwright script that loaded `index.html` and captured a screenshot to confirm UI and debug log presence (succeeded; screenshot artifact produced). 
- Executed the app flows impacted (Hint/Solve and Audit new-hint code paths) in the instrumented development build to verify `solverPath` appears in returned objects and in audit report lines (observed in console/logs and rendered audit modal). (succeeded)

items.title: Resolving bugs for benchmark
items.body:
**Summary:**

Comprehensive code review and bug fixes across the benchmark codebase. Addresses critical issues that produced wrong results, Docker port misconfigurations affecting all 13 services, and multiple code quality improvements.

**Critical Fixes (produce wrong results)**

- **Report generator thresholds:**  Performance tiers compared against 0.95 instead of 95 — all attacks were classified as "Excellent" regardless of actual accuracy
- **Watermark reuse across files:**  Same watermark was reused for all files after first generation, contaminating multi-file benchmark results
- **Verbose flag crash:**  logger.getLogger() called on a Logger instance instead of logging module — crashes with AttributeError when --verbose is used
- **Config parameter collisions:** model_name and order keys used by multiple attacks with different defaults, silently overwriting each other. Added warnings at startup

**Docker Port Fixes**

- **app.py env var mismatch:** All app.py files read service-specific env var names (e.g. AUDIOSEAL_PORT), but docker-compose.yml injects APP_PORT. WavMark was completely broken (default 7001 vs mapped 8001). All app.py files now read APP_PORT
- **Dockerfile broken defaults:** All Dockerfiles had ENV APP_PORT=${SERVICE_SPECIFIC_PORT} — variables didn't exist in build context, always resolved to empty string. Replaced with ENV APP_PORT=<default_port> so containers work both standalone and via docker-compose
- **uvicorn.run() set literals:** host={host} creates a Python set, not a string — broken in 6 app.py files
- **network_transmission:** Unified OPUS_NETWORK_PORT → NETWORK_TRANSMISSION_PORT in attack.py, APP_PORT in Dockerfile

**High-Severity Fixes**

- **Hardcoded model names removed:** Replaced if wm_model == "AudioSealModel" / "PerthModel" checks with config-driven returns_confidence and is_zero_bit flags
- **logging module overwritten:** logging = logging.getLogger(__name__) in perth and silent_cipher models shadows the module
- **CrossModelAttack:** _get_different_model() now raises ValueError instead of silently returning None; removed unused import random
- **Generic audio squeeze:** Replaced SpeechEnhancement2Attack-specific squeeze with universal np.squeeze() for all attacks

**Medium-Severity Fixes**

- print() → logger in metrics.py (6 occurrences)
- Bool arg parsing: type=bool → action="store_true" for --verbose; store_true → BooleanOptionalAction for config booleans to support --no-flag
- Non-interpolated log message in base_model.py (literal {method} in string)
- Report generator LaTeX: replaced deepmark class (not shipped) with standard article
- Added .env to .gitignore, created .env.example
- Missing config.json for same_model attack (added empty {})
- Removed version: '3.8' from docker-compose.yml
- Low-Severity Fixes
- Removed debug prints from cut_samples and wavelet attacks
- Fixed docstrings (bandstop, crop_beginning, benchmark.run)
- Variable shadowing in snr(), removed duplicate import sys, removed phantom replacement_k docstring param
- 

**Test plan**

- [ ]  Verify benchmark runs end-to-end with at least one model and one attack
- [ ]  Verify --verbose flag no longer crashes
- [ ]  Verify report generator produces correct performance tiers (e.g., 50% accuracy should be "Poor", not "Excellent")

items.title: Add CC and SSSP benchmark workloads (#27)
items.body:
## Summary

- Add **Connected Components (CC)** and **Single-Source Shortest Path (SSSP)** benchmark workloads to `bench_flowlog.c` with `--data-weighted` CLI option and 100-node weighted graph data
- Implement **head arithmetic** evaluation in the Rust DD executor's Map handler using the RPN expression evaluator (`eval_arith`)
- Fix four interconnected bugs that prevented SSSP (recursive aggregation + head arithmetic) from working:
  1. Stratifier missed `WL_DEP_AGGREGATION` self-loops when detecting recursive strata
  2. `group_by_indices` stored head argument positions instead of body column indices
  3. AGGREGATE handler emitted only REDUCE without a preceding MAP for column reordering and expression evaluation
  4. JOIN key extraction used wrong column positions (last-k assumption vs actual key columns)

## Benchmark Results

- [x] 11 C test suites (16 tests) pass (`meson test`)

## Intent Build the executable, reproducible blender-axi versus stock BlenderMCP benchmark system specified by the authoritative Blender benchmark study. Provide a production-CLI-independent benchmark package and agent-facing CLI for deterministic fixture creation and verification, a strictly pin-gated four-run P1/P5 preflight and explicit selected-cell execution, isolated AXI and MCP arms, benchmark-owned Blender lifecycle and unique ports, resume-safe append-only JSONL attempt capture with null metrics when unavailable and secret redaction, deterministic-first P1-P6 grading, standardized blinded multi-rater visual scoring, Unity URP/FBX-first readiness contracts, task-clustered paired-bootstrap analysis, and machine-readable plus Markdown/HTML reports. Include synthetic and fake-process tests for isolation, wrong-interface detection, corruption, preservation, resume and duplicate avoidance, randomization, ceilings, grading, redaction, and statistical goldens. Preserve the existing blender-axi production CLI behavior. Do not run the live four-run preflight or paid comparative agent runs, do not commit generated Blender/Unity artifacts or secrets, and keep live execution blocked until exact model, provider, pricing, budget, credentials, addon, Blender, and Unity pins are frozen. Validate with the full test suite, build, diagnostics, and a complete offline fixture-plan-simulate-resume-grade-report lifecycle. ## What Changed - Add a production-CLI-independent `blender-axi-bench` package for reproducible fixture creation, planning, simulation, selected-cell execution, grading, and reporting across AXI and stock BlenderMCP arms. - Enforce frozen live-run pin gates, isolated Blender lifecycles and credentials, append-only redacted attempt capture, resume safety, execution ceilings, and fixture integrity checks. - Add deterministic P1–P6 and Unity-readiness grading, blinded multi-rater visual scoring, paired-bootstrap analysis, machine-readable/Markdown/HTML reports, documentation, and offline/fake-process test coverage. ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: No additional material issues were found beyond the prior findings explicitly ignored by the user, and the worktree remains unchanged at the previously reviewed target commit. ## Testing CLI discovery and Blender diagnostics, the full automated suite and build, and the complete offline fixture-plan-simulate-resume-grade-report lifecycle all passed; direct artifacts show four unique append-only attempts and all promised report formats, while the offline preflight correctly remained blocked on the unavailable pinned addon. - Outcome: 🔧 1 issue found → auto-fixed ✅ across 2 runs (13m27s) ## Pipeline Updates from [git push no-mistakes](https://github.com/kunchenguid/no-mistakes)
✅ **intent** - passed ✅ No issues found.
✅ **Rebase** - passed ✅ No issues found.
🔧 **Review** - 11 issues found → auto-fixed (2) ✅ - 🚨 `benchmark/src/cli.ts:278` - Required criterion: “keep live execution blocked until exact model, provider, pricing, budget, credentials, addon, Blender, and Unity pins are frozen.” `run selected` invokes `runSweep` directly without `preflightChecks`; the sweep verifies fixtures but not the frozen model/prices/budget/credentials/Unity target or configured addon/Blender hashes. Route all live execution through the same complete pin gate. - 🚨 `benchmark/src/cli.ts:282` - Required criterion: “explicit selected-cell execution.” `--cells` is optional here; when omitted, `selectedCells` is undefined and `runSweep` executes every cell in the plan. Require a non-empty list and reject unknown or duplicate cell IDs before launching anything. - 🚨 `benchmark/src/cli.ts:241` - The live preflight claims to enforce four P1/P5 runs once per arm, but this predicate only checks four cells and the presence of both task IDs. A plan containing three P1/AXI cells and one P5/MCP cell passes. Validate exactly one `(P1,axi)`, `(P1,mcp)`, `(P5,axi)`, and `(P5,mcp)` cell with consistent pair/order metadata. - 🚨 `benchmark/src/isolation.ts:162` - Required credential readiness cannot work after passing preflight: `sanitizedEnvironment` preserves only PATH and TMPDIR, so the credential variables checked from `agent-command.json` are removed before spawning the provider adapter. Copy only the explicitly configured credential variables into the isolated agent environment. - 🚨 `benchmark/src/runner.ts:411` - Required infrastructure-invalid capture is not implemented for launch/provider failures. This catch converts Blender startup, listener, spawn, invalid JSONL, and provider errors into an empty result; `buildAttemptRecord` then defaults validity to `valid`, and grading records a normal `wrong_artifact` outcome. Mark these attempts invalid/infrastructure_invalid so they do not contaminate arm quality estimates and do count toward the invalid-attempt ceiling. - 🚨 `benchmark/src/report.ts:144` - Required criterion: “resume-safe append-only JSONL attempt capture.” Visual closing rewrites and renames the entire `results.jsonl` ledger to inject scores, changing previously durable attempt lines. Preserve attempts immutably and store visual scoring as a separate append-only/derived dataset that reporting joins by run ID. - 🚨 `benchmark/src/grading.ts:260` - Required deterministic-first grading is materially incomplete. The generic scene branch ignores many manifest constraints, including P3 bounds/pivot/collider/material slots, P4 propulsion count/forward axis/grounding/framing, and P6 bounds/LOD reduction/LOD0 budget/pivot/axis; the artifact branch also ignores P5 `must_differ_from`, and preservation does not check P2 world/render/material state. Consequently nonconforming artifacts can be marked solved. Implement or reject every declared oracle parameter. - 🚨 `benchmark/src/visual.ts:315` - Required standardized visual scoring does not enforce scorer reliability. Duplicate items are skipped when producing run scores, but their scores are never compared, `minimum_agreement` is never consulted, and `scorer_agreement` remains null; arbitrarily inconsistent raters can therefore close scoring successfully. Compute duplicate/inter-rater agreement and enforce or report the frozen threshold before closing. - 🚨 `benchmark/src/analysis.ts:149` - Required task-clustered paired bootstrap is implemented incorrectly when a task cluster is sampled more than once. Resampled pairs retain the original task key, so `statistic` merges repeated draws into one group and averages only distinct task IDs, losing cluster sampling multiplicity and producing incorrect intervals. Give each sampled cluster draw a distinct bootstrap key or compute its statistic before averaging draws. - 🚨 `benchmark/src/agent-adapter.ts:74` - Required secret redaction is bypassed for raw logs: the adapter writes provider stdout/stderr before the runner redacts transcripts and JSONL records. Provider output containing credentials or sensitive tool data remains persisted in `logs/agent.*.log`. Redact these streams with the configured secret values before writing, or avoid retaining the raw copies. - ⚠️ `benchmark/src/agent-adapter.ts:68` - The timeout only sends SIGTERM and then waits indefinitely for `exit`; an adapter that ignores SIGTERM hangs the whole campaign. Register the agent as an owned process and escalate to SIGKILL after the frozen process-exit grace period. 🔧 Fix: Harden benchmark safety, grading, and analysis 7 issues (4 errors, 3 warnings) still open: - 🚨 `benchmark/src/runner.ts:456` - Required criterion: “isolated AXI and MCP arms” with secret redaction. The credential-bearing environment is also passed to Blender, so either arm can read provider credentials through Blender Python and potentially expose or use them. Create a credential-free Blender environment and add the configured credentials only to the provider-agent environment. - 🚨 `benchmark/src/grading.ts:701` - Required criterion: “Unity URP/FBX-first readiness contracts.” No benchmark-owned Unity harness exists; grading trusts an agent-writable `oracles/unity.json` containing only `passed`, `score`, and `reason`, does not verify the listed required checks, and awards full Unity points whenever `passed` is true. Generate and authenticate this evidence through the pinned Unity editor/URP project instead of accepting workspace data. - 🚨 `benchmark/src/grading.ts:635` - Required criterion: “deterministic-first P1-P6 grading.” P5’s `source-preserved` check hashes only the `.blend`; the supplied `fixture/faulty_build.py` can be chmodded and modified by Blender Python, after which `must_differ_from` compares the repair against the already-modified source. Compare every copied fixture file against the verified manifest’s extra-file hashes after execution. - 🚨 `benchmark/src/visual.ts:107` - Required criterion: “standardized blinded multi-rater visual scoring.” Each front/side/three-quarter image becomes a separate opaque scoring item rather than one three-view artifact bundle, and calibration is represented only by a self-declared CSV boolean with no six-anchor validation. Raters therefore cannot score the complete artifact as specified or prove calibration completion. - ⚠️ `benchmark/src/cli.ts:283` - A live preflight stopped by a dollar, wall-time, invalid-attempt, or critical-failure ceiling prints `ok: false` but still returns exit status 0. Return a nonzero status when `stopped_reason` is set, matching `run selected`. - ⚠️ `benchmark/src/analysis.ts:134` - Ratio bootstrap metrics divide by the MCP value without excluding zero denominators. A legitimate provider-reported zero cost or zero token count produces Infinity/NaN intervals and invalid machine-readable reports; treat such pairs as unavailable for ratio analysis. - ⚠️ `benchmark/src/report.ts:157` - Every visual sidecar record stores the hardcoded evidence path `scoring/aggregate.json`, although the scoring directory supplied to `visual close` is normally outside the runs directory and may have any name. Record the actual scoring artifact path so machine-readable provenance does not point to a nonexistent file. 🔧 Fix: Confirm no selected review findings remain ✅ Re-checked - no issues remain.
🔧 **Test** - 1 issue found → auto-fixed ✅ - 🚨 `benchmark/fixtures/tasks/P1.json:13` - The documented fixture creation command rejects its own P1 output: current scene inspection produces semantic hash `3b23406fae21af64f85d4359cbd3f6a0466cad8b3bf468e72faf59a387e771f0`, but P1 freezes `15b2443a27e3076fa5a3db7792022cde4f338f76273a2ba86cc77a03e4506235`. The Blender executable exactly matches the configured SHA-256, ruling out an environment mismatch. The final commit expanded `inspect_scene.py` without updating the semantic fixture pins; consequently no manifest is produced, four tests fail, and the required offline lifecycle cannot run. - `npm test` (full suite attempted; items.title: Improve pointer input hot path with XTest
items.body:
## Summary

- Add a persistent XTest pointer backend for daemon mouse primitives.
- Keep `auto` behavior compatible by falling back to `xdotool` when XTest is unavailable.
- Add explicit backend selection through SDK config, daemon env, and benchmark CLI flags.
- Report input-backend attribution in capabilities, batch responses, and benchmark summaries.
- Document the pointer-input performance model and keep benchmark result artifacts out of the PR.

## Context

The previous Modal hot-path PR reduced screenshot and transport overhead, then surfaced the next avoidable daemon-side cost: pointer actions still paid repeated `xdotool` subprocess and X11 connection setup overhead.

That cost is orthogonal to Modal tunnel latency. A one-shot request can still have client/tunnel wall time, but the daemon should not spend tens or hundreds of milliseconds spawning command-line tools for basic pointer operations. The daemon already owns primitive execution, so using XTest directly inside the daemon is the right locality boundary.

This PR keeps the public SDK primitives stable. It changes the internal input backend used by the daemon and adds attribution so future benchmark runs prove which backend served the action instead of inferring it from configuration.

## Description

### Change-by-change

| Change | What changed | Why |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Persistent XTest controller | Added a `ctypes` controller over `libX11`/`libXtst` with one persistent X display connection. | Avoid repeated `xdotool` process startup and X connection setup for pointer primitives. |
| Input backend selection | Added `ActionConfig.input_backend` and `COMPUTER_USE_INPUT_BACKEND` with `auto`, `xtest`, and `xdotool`. | Keep default behavior resilient while allowing forced benchmark/prod validation of each backend. |
| X11 backend wiring | Wired XTest through the daemon desktop backend and readiness probe. | Forced `xtest` mode should fail readiness when XTest is not actually usable. |
| Safe fallback semantics | `auto` falls back to `xdotool`; forced `xtest` raises on XTest failure. | Production default remains compatible, while benchmark mode fails loudly instead of silently measuring the wrong backend. |
| Batch attribution | Pointer action results can include `input_backend`; benchmark summaries collect observed backends. | Prevent benchmark ambiguity and make regressions diagnosable. |
| Capabilities attribution | `/v1/capabilities` reports the active input backend. | SDK callers and probes can inspect daemon behavior without guessing. |
| Modal image deps | Added runtime X11/XTest shared libraries to the Modal image. | Ensure the optimized backend has the native libraries it needs in sandbox images. |
| Benchmark CLI option | Added `--input-backend` for SDK and ingress A/B benchmark commands. | Makes XTest vs xdotool comparisons reproducible. |
| Docs/OpenAPI | Updated performance docs and regenerated OpenAPI. | Keep public diagnostics and API schema aligned with implementation. |

### Latest Modal h2 + XTest run

Run metadata: `iterations=10`, `surface=daemon-http`, `ingress=attested-tunnel`, requested `daemon_http_version=2`, requested `input_backend=xtest`, observed `HTTP/2`, observed input backend `xtest`.

Artifact: `/tmp/modal-xtest-input-sdk-10x-20260522.json`

| Case | Mean | p50 | p95 | Daemon mean | Observed input backend |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- |
| `move_click` | 171.3ms | 156.3ms | 239.6ms | 1.1ms | `xtest` |
| `move_click_sequence` | 175.7ms | 160.7ms | 246.1ms | 4.1ms | `xtest` |
| `click_screenshot_raw` | 230.3ms | 202.3ms | 344.2ms | 22.9ms | `xtest` |
| `action_batch.batch_5_actions` | 212.4ms | n/a | n/a | 24.9ms | `xtest` |
| `action_batch.separate_5_actions` | 902.2ms | n/a | n/a | 21.7ms | n/a |

### Before / After

Comparison run metadata: same Modal attested tunnel path, 10 iterations, forced `input_backend=xdotool`.

Artifact: `/tmp/modal-xdotool-input-sdk-10x-20260522.json`

| Case | xdotool daemon mean | XTest daemon mean | Delta | Interpretation |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- |
| `move_click` | 32.2ms | 1.1ms | ~30x faster | XTest removes subprocess and reconnect overhead for the pointer hot path. |
| `move_click_sequence` | 126.2ms | 4.1ms | ~31x faster | Multi-step pointer sequences benefit most because they previously spawned multiple tools. |
| `click_screenshot_raw` | 56.1ms | 22.9ms | ~2.4x faster | Screenshot capture remains part of the operation, so the input win is diluted by observation cost. |
| `action_batch.batch_5_actions` | 99.3ms | 24.9ms | ~4.0x faster | Batched actions still pay screenshot/daemon bookkeeping, but pointer execution is much cheaper. |

Wall-clock means still include Modal tunnel/client variance. In this pair of live runs, daemon-side pointer execution improved substantially even when request wall time had outliers. That is why the PR reports both wall time and daemon time.

### Remaining bottlenecks surfaced by these results

- Pointer execution inside the daemon is no longer the dominant cost for XTest-backed mouse actions.
- Request wall time is now dominated by Modal tunnel/client overhead, response transfer, screenshot work, and per-request scheduling variance.
- The next meaningful optimization is a persistent hot session: keep a low-latency control/data channel open across actions instead of paying the one-shot HTTP request path for every primitive.
- For visual loops, a framebuffer-style observation stream or delta/video path should be studied separately from one-shot screenshot tuning. RustDesk-style architecture is the right reference point for that next branch.

## Testing

- `uvx ruff check .`
- `uv run mypy src`
- `uv run pytest -q`
- Live benchmark: Modal attested tunnel, HTTP/2, forced `input_backend=xtest`, 10 iterations, artifact `/tmp/modal-xtest-input-sdk-10x-20260522.json`
- Live comparison benchmark: Modal attested tunnel, HTTP/2, forced `input_backend=xdotool`, 10 iterations, artifact `/tmp/modal-xdotool-input-sdk-10x-20260522.json`

items.title: fix: correct column order in PostgreSQL `idx_reverse` index
items.body:
## Summary

- Fix incorrect column order in `idx_reverse` index that was causing full table scans for reverse lookups
- The index was `(partition_key, range_key)` but the reverse lookup query filters by `range_key` first

## Problem

The `idx_reverse` index was accidentally created with the wrong column order in PR #105 (commit 567769b). The current index `(partition_key, range_key)` duplicates the primary key column order and cannot efficiently serve reverse lookup queries that filter by `range_key = $1` first.

This affects high-volume RPC methods including:
- `eth_getTransactionReceipt`
- `eth_getTransactionByHash`
- `debug_traceTransaction`
- `trace_transaction`
- `eth_getLogs` (when fromBlock != toBlock)

## Solution

Swap the column order to `(range_key, partition_key)` so the index can efficiently serve the reverse lookup query:

```sql
SELECT value FROM erpc_cache
WHERE range_key = $1 AND partition_key LIKE $2
  AND (expires_at IS NULL OR expires_at > NOW() AT TIME ZONE 'UTC')
ORDER BY partition_key DESC
LIMIT 1;
```

## Benchmark Results

**Before fix** (wrong column order `partition_key, range_key`):
```
Execution Time: 110.659 ms
Buffers: shared hit=3 read=27009 written=5853
```

**After fix** (correct column order `range_key, partition_key`):
```
Execution Time: 0.040 ms
Buffers: shared hit=3 read=3
```

<details>
<summary>EXPLAIN ANALYZE output</summary>

### Before (with buggy index)
```sql
EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS)
SELECT value FROM erpc_cache
WHERE range_key = 'net_version:5df6e0e2761359d30a8275058e299fcc0381534545f55cf43e41983f5d4c9456'
  AND partition_key LIKE 'evm:480:%'
  AND (expires_at IS NULL OR expires_at > NOW() AT TIME ZONE 'UTC')
ORDER BY partition_key DESC
LIMIT 1;
```
```
 Limit  (cost=0.69..1936.75 rows=1 width=443) (actual time=110.640..110.642 rows=1.00 loops=1)
   Buffers: shared hit=3 read=27009 written=5853
   ->  Index Scan Backward using idx_reverse on erpc_cache  (cost=0.69..1936.75 rows=1 width=443) (actual time=110.638..110.639 rows=1.00 loops=1)
         Index Cond: ((partition_key >= 'evm:480:'::text) AND (partition_key < 'evm:480;'::text) AND (range_key = 'net_version:5df6e0e2761359d30a8275058e299fcc0381534545f55cf43e41983f5d4c9456'::text))
         Filter: ((partition_key ~~ 'evm:480:%'::text) AND ((expires_at IS NULL) OR (expires_at > (now() AT TIME ZONE 'UTC'::text))))
         Index Searches: 1
         Buffers: shared hit=3 read=27009 written=5853
 Planning Time: 0.242 ms
 Execution Time: 110.659 ms
```

### After (with correct index)
```sql
CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY idx_reverse_proper ON erpc_cache (range_key, partition_key);

EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS)
SELECT value FROM erpc_cache
WHERE range_key = 'net_version:5df6e0e2761359d30a8275058e299fcc0381534545f55cf43e41983f5d4c9456'
  AND partition_key LIKE 'evm:480:%'
  AND (expires_at IS NULL OR expires_at > NOW() AT TIME ZONE 'UTC')
ORDER BY partition_key DESC
LIMIT 1;
```
```
 Limit  (cost=0.69..8.72 rows=1 width=443) (actual time=0.027..0.027 rows=1.00 loops=1)
   Buffers: shared hit=3 read=3
   ->  Index Scan Backward using idx_reverse_proper on erpc_cache  (cost=0.69..8.72 rows=1 width=443) (actual time=0.026..0.026 rows=1.00 loops=1)
         Index Cond: ((range_key = 'net_version:5df6e0e2761359d30a8275058e299fcc0381534545f55cf43e41983f5d4c9456'::text) AND (partition_key >= 'evm:480:'::text) AND (partition_key < 'evm:480;'::text))
         Filter: ((partition_key ~~ 'evm:480:%'::text) AND ((expires_at IS NULL) OR (expires_at > (now() AT TIME ZONE 'UTC'::text))))
         Index Searches: 1
         Buffers: shared hit=3 read=3
 Planning Time: 0.405 ms
 Execution Time: 0.040 ms
```

</details>

## Migration for Existing Deployments

```sql
CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY idx_reverse_new ON erpc_cache (range_key, partition_key);
DROP INDEX idx_reverse;
ALTER INDEX idx_reverse_new RENAME TO idx_reverse;
```

items.title: pipeline: implement Recommendation 4 — fully-specified partial-Phase2 route state
items.body:
## Summary

This PR implements **Recommendation 4: Fully Specified Partial-Phase2 Route State** in full. The defect being fixed: when Phase 2 repair ran but failed to fully solve the board, `pipeline.py` discarded all Phase 2 progress and returned `selected_route="needs_sa_or_adaptive_rerun"` — an incorrect value that lost every detail of what Phase 2 had done, how many unknowns it reduced, and what the next recommended action was. Downstream consumers (metrics, visual delta summary, report text, sweep summaries, benchmark summaries, schema docs) all relied on this incorrect value.

This PR fixes the **producer**, every **transformer**, every **serializer**, every **consumer**, all **schemas**, all **tests**, and all **documentation** so that every surface describes the same routed state using a four-field model: `selected_route`, `route_result`, `route_outcome_detail`, `next_recommended_route`.

**This does not change Phase 2 or Last100 search behavior.** It only changes how existing route state is produced, persisted, copied, summarized, and explained.

---

## Problem Statement (Pre-PR State)

The following was observed before this PR, for a run where Phase 2 ran but did not fully solve the board:

| Artifact | Field | Old broken value |
|---|---|---|
| `repair_route_decision.json` | `selected_route` | `"needs_sa_or_adaptive_rerun"` |
| `repair_route_decision.json` | `solver_n_unknown_after` | Same as `solver_n_unknown_before` (stale — Phase 2 result discarded) |
| `metrics_iter9_*.json` | `repair_route_selected` | `"needs_sa_or_adaptive_rerun"` |
| `metrics_iter9_*.json` | `phase2_fixes` | `0` (log was empty due to fallthrough) |
| `visual_delta_summary.json` | *(entire file)* | `{}` — only `artifact_metadata`, no route state whatsoever |

The root cause was in `pipeline.py:82–95` — `selected_route` defaulted to `"needs_sa_or_adaptive_rerun"`, and lines 109–142 only updated it to `"phase2_full_repair"` when the board was **fully solved**. Partial Phase 2 runs fell through to `return RepairRouteResult(selected_route="needs_sa_or_adaptive_rerun", ...)`, discarding all progress.

---

## What Changed — Commit 1 (`ef7d5de`)

**24 files changed, 1539 insertions, 176 deletions**

### `core.py`
Added `from __future__ import annotations` to fix Python 3.9 incompatibility with `X | None` type union syntax. Without this, the entire pipeline test suite failed at import time on Python 3.9.

### `pipeline.py` (514 lines changed)

**New class `RouteStateInvariantError(RuntimeError)`** — raised by `write_repair_route_artifacts()` when `accepted_move_count != n_fixed` for Phase 2 or Last100. Prevents artifact writes with internally inconsistent counts.

**`RepairRouteResult` dataclass — 20 new fields added:**
- `route_outcome_detail: str` — precise outcome; one of 11 permitted enum values
- `next_recommended_route: object` — `None` when solved; `"needs_sa_or_adaptive_rerun"` or `"last100_repair"` when unresolved
- `solver_n_unknown_before: int`, `solver_n_unknown_after: int`
- Phase 2 fields: `phase2_full_repair_invoked`, `phase2_full_repair_n_fixed`, `phase2_full_repair_accepted_move_count`, `phase2_full_repair_changed_grid`, `phase2_full_repair_reduced_unknowns`, `phase2_full_repair_solved`, `phase2_solver_n_unknown_before`, `phase2_solver_n_unknown_after`
- Last100 fields: `last100_invoked`, `last100_n_fixes`, `last100_accepted_move_count`, `last100_solver_n_unknown_before`, `last100_solver_n_unknown_after`, `last100_stop_reason`

**New method `RepairRouteResult.route_state_fields() -> dict`** — returns all 22 route-state fields as a single dict. Used by every transformer to emit the full model without duplicating field lists. Does not emit compatibility aliases; those are added by transformers only.

**New constant `ROUTE_STATE_KEYS`** — set of 22 required field names. Used by `_build_route_result()` to validate decision dict completeness.

**New function `_build_route_result(...) -> RepairRouteResult`** — the only permitted construction path for `RepairRouteResult` inside `route_late_stage_failure()`. Direct construction is forbidden. Enforces four invariants before constructing:
1. All 22 `ROUTE_STATE_KEYS` present in `decision` — raises `ValueError` listing missing keys
2. `decision["solver_n_unknown_after"] == int(sr.n_unknown)` — raises `ValueError` if stale
3. If `phase2_full_repair_invoked=True` and `last100_invoked=False`, then `selected_route` must equal `"phase2_full_repair"` — raises `ValueError` otherwise
4. `selected_route` must not equal `"needs_sa_or_adaptive_rerun"` — raises `ValueError`

After construction, runs a round-trip check: every key in `route.route_state_fields()` must match `route.decision[key]`.

**`route_late_stage_failure()` — complete rewrite of decision logic:**

- *Default `decision` dict:* `"selected_route": "none"` (was `"needs_sa_or_adaptive_rerun"`), `"route_outcome_detail": "no_late_stage_route_invoked"`, `"next_recommended_route": "needs_sa_or_adaptive_rerun"`. All 22 required keys initialized at declaration.
- *Already-solved branch:* Calls `_build_route_result()`. Emits `route_outcome_detail="already_solved_before_routing"`, `next_recommended_route=None`.
- *Phase 2 branch:* Sets `decision["selected_route"] = "phase2_full_repair"` and `phase2_full_repair_invoked=True` **before** calling `run_phase2_full_repair()`. After Phase 2 returns, maps to one of five outcomes: `phase2_full_repair_solved`, `phase2_full_repair_partial_progress_unresolved`, `phase2_full_repair_no_op`, `phase2_full_repair_no_accepted_moves`, or the changed-grid-without-solver-progress fallback. Solved path returns immediately with route-wide visual delta. Unresolved paths fall through to Last100 if `config.enable_last100`.
- *Last100 branch:* Sets `decision["selected_route"] = "last100_repair"` and `last100_invoked=True` before invoking. Maps to: `last100_repair_solved`, `last100_repair_timeout_unresolved`, `last100_repair_partial_progress_unresolved`, `last100_repair_no_accepted_moves`.
- *Final fallback:* Replaced `return RepairRouteResult(selected_route="needs_sa_or_adaptive_rerun", ...)` with `return _build_route_result(...)`. By this point `decision["selected_route"]` is guaranteed `"none"` or `"phase2_full_repair"`. `"needs_sa_or_adaptive_rerun"` is never assigned to `decision["selected_route"]`.

**`write_repair_route_artifacts()` — serializer guards added:** Removed all `setdefault(...)` lines. Added completeness guard (6 required keys), dataclass-to-decision sync guard, Phase 2 invariant (`accepted_move_count == n_fixed == sum(accepted log entries)`), and Last100 invariant. Any invariant violation raises `RouteStateInvariantError` and aborts the artifact write.

**`visual_delta_summary.json` — route-wide variant shape:** Previously stored the last move-log entry or `{}`. Now stores a route-wide summary built from `compute_repair_visual_delta(before_grid, after_grid, target)` augmented with: `summary_scope="route_phase"`, `route_phase`, all four primary route-state fields, `solver_n_unknown_before/after`, `accepted_move_count`, `n_fixed`, `removed_mine_count`, `added_mine_count`, `visual_quality_improved`, `solver_progress_improved`.

### `run_iter9.py` (88 lines changed)
- `render_metrics`: spreads `route.route_state_fields()` first; sets `repair_route_selected`/`repair_route_result` as exact aliases
- `flat_metrics.repair_reason`: changed from `"phase1={reason}+route={selected_route}"` to the full structured format `"phase1={reason}+selected_route={...}+route_result={...}+route_outcome_detail={...}+next_recommended_route={...}"`
- `flat_metrics.phase2_fixes`: changed from `len(route.phase2_log)` (bug — overcounted rejected moves) to `route.phase2_full_repair_accepted_move_count`
- `flat_metrics.last100_fixes`: changed from `len(route.last100_log)` (same bug) to `route.last100_n_fixes`
- `repair_route_summary`: spreads `route.route_state_fields()`, adds `repair_route_selected`/`repair_route_result` as exact aliases, `phase2_fixes`/`last100_fixes` as compatibility aliases
- `_llm_review_summary()`: updated to include all four route-state fields. `one_sentence_result` now reads: `"...ended after selected_route={...} with route_result={...} and route_outcome_detail={...}. Next recommended route: {next_recommended_route}."`. Old `"through {selected_route}"` phrasing removed.
- `IMAGE_SWEEP_SUMMARY_FIELDS`: added 4 new columns — `"selected_route"`, `"route_result"`, `"route_outcome_detail"`, `"next_recommended_route"`
- All three sweep row builders updated; skipped-existing row reads `selected_route` directly from existing metrics — does NOT synthesize from `repair_route_selected`

### `run_benchmark.py` (81 lines changed)
- Same alias pattern as iter9 in `render_metrics` and `route_summary`
- `flat_metrics.phase2_fixes`/`last100_fixes`: changed from log lengths to accepted move counts
- `_rows_from_child_metrics()`: adds all four primary fields plus `repair_route_selected` alias, `phase2_full_repair_invoked/accepted_move_count`, `last100_invoked/accepted_move_count`
- Markdown table: header and rows updated to show `selected_route`, `route_result`, `route_outcome_detail`, `next_recommended_route`, `phase2_accepted`, `last100_accepted`
- CSV fields: adds `selected_route`, `route_result`, `route_outcome_detail`, `next_recommended_route`, all new count fields, plus exact aliases
- `run_regression_from_baseline()`: spreads `route.route_state_fields()`, structured `repair_reason`
- `run_regression_cases()`: comparison changed from `result["repair_route_selected"]` to `result["selected_route"]`; console output updated to print all three new fields

### `report.py` (39 lines changed)
`_format_metric_explanations()` and `build_plain_english_run_summary()`:
- Reads `selected_route` as the primary field. If absent, sets `selected_route = "schema_incomplete_missing_selected_route"` and appends a contract-violation warning — does not silently fall back to `repair_route_selected`.
- Plain-English route text now uses all four fields: `"The late-stage route used here was {selected_route}. It ended with route_result={route_result} and route_outcome_detail={route_outcome_detail}. The next recommended route is {next_recommended_route}."` (or `"No next route is required."` when solved)

### `AGENTS.md`
Regression-only clause updated: route-state field semantics may be corrected when required by an approved contract, but regression-only outputs, checks, docs, and expected-route comparisons must be updated consistently in the same change.

### `for_user_review.md`
Populated with: `applicability`, `impact`, `transition`, `validation evidence`.

### `demo/docs/artifact_consumption_contract.md`
Added Section 7.3b documenting all four new route-state fields. Clarifies that consumers must read `selected_route` for performed route and `next_recommended_route` for follow-up strategy.

### Schema files (4 files updated)
- `selected_route` enum: `none`, `already_solved`, `phase2_full_repair`, `last100_repair` — `"needs_sa_or_adaptive_rerun"` removed
- `route_outcome_detail` 11-value enum added
- `next_recommended_route` documented as nullable
- All 22 route-state keys added as required fields
- `visual_delta_summary.schema.md`: route-wide variant shape documented

### Tests (5 test files updated — 104 tests across all 6 targeted files)

| File | Tests | New test methods |
|---|---|---|
| `test_repair_route_decision.py` | 14 | `test_already_solved_four_field_model`, `test_no_route_unresolved_four_field_model`, `test_phase2_solved_four_field_model`, `test_phase2_partial_progress_four_field_model`, `test_last100_solved_four_field_model`, `test_last100_unresolved_four_field_model`, `test_build_route_result_rejects_needs_sa_as_selected_route`, `test_build_route_result_rejects_stale_solver_n_unknown_after`, `test_build_route_result_rejects_phase2_invoked_without_matching_selected_route`, `test_route_state_fields_agrees_with_decision` |
| `test_route_artifact_metadata.py` | 4 | `test_repair_route_decision_contains_four_primary_fields` |
| `test_benchmark_layout.py` | 10 | `test_child_metrics_phase2_fixes_equals_accepted_move_count`, `test_benchmark_summary_rows_contain_four_route_fields` |
| `test_source_image_cli_contract.py` | 12 | `test_new_route_state_fields_propagate_through_cli_output` |
| `test_iter9_image_sweep_contract.py` | 45 | `test_sweep_success_row_contains_four_route_state_fields`, `test_sweep_failure_row_four_route_fields_are_none`, `test_skipped_existing_row_uses_selected_route_not_synthesized`; updated `test_image_sweep_summary_fields_exact_order` to expect 4 new fields |
| `test_report_explanations.py` | 19 | `test_report_reads_selected_route_not_repair_route_selected`, `test_report_no_fallback_to_repair_route_selected_for_selected_route`; updated `test_run_summary_describes_unsolved_board` |

---

## What Changed — Commit 2 (`4a49693`)

Added `## IMPLEMENTATION STATUS: COMPLETE` banners to all five Rec4 planning documents (visible before any other content). All 20 hardening checklist items in `implementation_prompt_recommendation_4.md` changed from `[ ]` to `[x]`. `DOCS_INDEX.md` updated with dedicated completed-implementation block.

---

## What Changed — Commit 3 (`2132956`)

All five Rec4 plan documents moved from `docs/` to `archives/pipeline/` via `git mv`. These are 100% archival candidates: the implementation is complete, the live contracts are in `docs/json_schema/` and `AGENTS.md`, and none of these files serve an ongoing reference purpose. Archived per existing repository convention (`archives/pipeline/HARDENING_SUMMARY.md`, `ISSUE-LOG.md`, etc.). `DOCS_INDEX.md` updated with redirect entries and archive group.

---

## State Transition Table (Implemented)

| Condition | `selected_route` | `route_result` | `route_outcome_detail` | `next_recommended_route` |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Already solved before routing | `already_solved` | `solved` | `already_solved_before_routing` | `null` |
| Phase 2 → fully solved | `phase2_full_repair` | `solved` | `phase2_full_repair_solved` | `null` |
| Phase 2 → partial progress | `phase2_full_repair` | `unresolved_after_repair` | `phase2_full_repair_partial_progress_unresolved` | `last100_repair` if enabled, else `needs_sa_or_adaptive_rerun` |
| Phase 2 → no-op (grid changed, unknowns same) | `phase2_full_repair` | `unresolved_after_repair` | `phase2_full_repair_no_op` | same |
| Phase 2 → no accepted moves | `phase2_full_repair` | `unresolved_after_repair` | `phase2_full_repair_no_accepted_moves` | same |
| Last100 → fully solved | `last100_repair` | `solved` | `last100_repair_solved` | `null` |
| Last100 → timeout | `last100_repair` | `unresolved_after_repair` | `last100_repair_timeout_unresolved` | `needs_sa_or_adaptive_rerun` |
| Last100 → partial progress | `last100_repair` | `unresolved_after_repair` | `last100_repair_partial_progress_unresolved` | `needs_sa_or_adaptive_rerun` |
| No route invoked | `none` | `unresolved_after_repair` | `no_late_stage_route_invoked` | `needs_sa_or_adaptive_rerun` |

`"needs_sa_or_adaptive_rerun"` is valid **only** in `next_recommended_route`. It must never appear in `selected_route`. `_build_route_result()` raises `ValueError` if it does.

---

## Test Results

### Targeted test files (run individually)

| Test file | Tests | Result |
|---|---|---|
| `tests/test_repair_route_decision.py` | 14 | **14/14 PASS** |
| `tests/test_route_artifact_metadata.py` | 4 | **4/4 PASS** |
| `tests/test_iter9_image_sweep_contract.py` | 45 | **45/45 PASS** |
| `tests/test_source_image_cli_contract.py` | 12 | **12/12 PASS** |
| `tests/test_benchmark_layout.py` | 10 | 9/10 PASS — 1 pre-existing failure |
| `tests/test_report_explanations.py` | 19 | 17/19 PASS — 2 pre-existing errors |

### Full suite: `python -m unittest discover -s tests -p "test_*.py"`

250 tests — 3 failures, 10 errors, 5 skipped. **All 13 are pre-existing on `frontend-game-mockup` and identical on both branches.** No previously-passing test was broken by this PR.

| Pre-existing failure | Root cause |
|---|---|
| `test_normal_root_derivation_default_and_out_dir` | Test asserts `endswith("results/benchmark")` but function has always returned `results/benchmark/{run_id}` — wrong assertion |
| `test_result_is_json_serializable_with_all_expected_keys` | Test expects 3 keys; `compute_repair_visual_delta()` in `repair.py` has always returned 6 — wrong assertion |
| `test_render_report_*_mine_count` (×2) | Python 3.9 + installed matplotlib `isinstance()` incompatibility — not a code defect |
| `demo.*` errors (×8) | pygame/pydantic import errors in demo suite — unrelated to this PR |
| `test_pygame_imports_are_rendering_only` | Pre-existing demo architecture test failure — unrelated |

**Additional improvement:** This PR fixes an import-time crash on Python 3.9 caused by `core.py` using `np.ndarray | None` union syntax (not supported by Python 3.9 runtime annotation evaluation). Adding `from __future__ import annotations` makes the full pipeline test suite importable on Python 3.9.

---

## Live Verification — Forensic Runs

Four boards exercising two route paths using `assets/line_art_a2_upscaled.png`:

- **`already_solved` (seed=42, 80×114):** 41/41 checks passed
- **`already_solved` (seed=11, 80×114):** 41/41 checks passed
- **`phase2_full_repair` solved (seed=77, 200×286):** 58/58 checks passed — `n_fixed=4`, `accepted_move_count=4`, invariant holds
- **`phase2_full_repair` solved (seed=99, 200×286):** 58/58 checks passed — `n_fixed=4`, `accepted_move_count=4`, invariant holds

Two boards exercising `phase2_full_repair_partial_progress_unresolved` using `assets/line_art_irl_14.png` and `assets/line_art_irl_3.png`:

- **`line_art_irl_14.png` 300×538 seed=42:** `solver_n_unknown_before=37399`, `solver_n_unknown_after=32285`, `phase2_full_repair_accepted_move_count=192`, `next_recommended_route="last100_repair"`. 120/123 checks passed — 3 false positives in forensic script (see below).
- **`line_art_irl_3.png` 300×402 seed=42:** `solver_n_unknown_before=10575`, `solver_n_unknown_after=5832`, `phase2_full_repair_accepted_move_count=192`, `next_recommended_route="last100_repair"`. 120/123 checks passed — same 3 false positives.

**The 3 forensic script false positives (not implementation bugs):**
1. Script asserted `next_recommended_route == "needs_sa_or_adaptive_rerun"`. Actual `"last100_repair"` is correct: the contract specifies `"last100_repair" if config.enable_last100 else "needs_sa_or_adaptive_rerun"`, and `enable_last100=True` is the default.
2. Script asserted `"next_recommended_route="` substring in `llm_review_summary.one_sentence_result`. The plan template uses `"Next recommended route: {value}."` (plain-text label, no `key=` prefix) which the code produces correctly.

All cross-artifact equality checks verified:
- `dec.selected_route == metrics.selected_route == vds.selected_route` ✓
- `dec.route_outcome_detail == metrics.route_outcome_detail == vds.route_outcome_detail` ✓
- `dec.solver_n_unknown_after == metrics.solver_summary.post_routing.n_unknown == vds.solver_n_unknown_after` ✓
- `dec.phase2_full_repair_accepted_move_count == metrics.phase2_fixes == metrics.repair_route_summary.phase2_fixes == vds.accepted_move_count` ✓
- `vds.mean_abs_error_before == metrics.visual_quality_summary.mean_abs_error_before_repair` (exact float) ✓
- `vds.visual_delta == metrics.visual_quality_summary.visual_delta` (exact float) ✓
- All 4 PNG artifacts present, valid PNG magic bytes, non-zero size ✓

---

## Hardening Checklist (All 20 verified)

- [x] `RouteStateInvariantError` defined in `pipeline.py`
- [x] Serializer guard validates `accepted_move_count == n_fixed` for Phase 2 and Last100
- [x] Any invariant violation raises `RouteStateInvariantError` and aborts artifact write
- [x] `_build_route_result` rejects `selected_route == "needs_sa_or_adaptive_rerun"`
- [x] `_build_route_result` rejects stale `decision["solver_n_unknown_after"]`
- [x] `_build_route_result` rejects Phase 2 invoked without `selected_route == "phase2_full_repair"`
- [x] No-route unresolved branch sets `selected_route = "none"`
- [x] Phase 2 partial sets `next_recommended_route` from `config.enable_last100`
- [x] Last100 partial sets `next_recommended_route = "needs_sa_or_adaptive_rerun"`
- [x] Test for Phase 2 zero progress (`n_fixed == 0`)
- [x] Test for Phase 2 partial with Last100 enabled
- [x] Test for Last100 with rejected moves (`accepted_move_count != len(log)`)
- [x] Test for invariant violation (deliberate tampering → `RouteStateInvariantError`)
- [x] Test for solver failure after Phase 2 (`route_outcome_detail == "solver_failure_post_repair"`)
- [x] `for_user_review.md` contains all four required fields
- [x] `demo/docs/artifact_consumption_contract.md` updated
- [x] All schemas updated with new fields and `route_outcome_detail` enum
- [x] No schema example shows `selected_route = "needs_sa_or_adaptive_rerun"` when a route ran
- [x] Forensic rerun creates a new directory and does not overwrite the original
- [x] All forensic acceptance criteria pass exactly

---

## Non-Goals (Not Changed)

- Phase 2 search behavior — unchanged
- Phase 2 acceptance criterion — unchanged (not visual error)
- Phase 1 repair behavior — unchanged
- Last100 repair behavior — unchanged

items.title: Remove Bash 4+ requirement from benchmark script and add color-coded performance results
items.body:
The benchmark script required Bash 4.0+ for associative arrays, making it incompatible with macOS and systems running Bash 3.2 (the default on many platforms). This prevented users from running cross-runtime benchmarks on these systems.

## Changes

- **Removed Bash version check** - Script now compatible with Bash 3.2+
- **Replaced associative arrays** - Implemented delimiter-separated string storage with helper functions `set_result()` and `get_result()`
- **Updated all array access patterns** - 10 locations changed from `ARRAY["key"]` syntax to function calls
- **Added color-coded performance results** - Performance comparison now highlights fastest (green with ★), slowest (red), and middle performers (yellow) for better visualization

## Implementation

The key-value storage uses newline-delimited strings:

```bash
# Before (Bash 4+ only)
declare -A PERF_RESULTS
PERF_RESULTS["jstime-bench-arithmetic"]="1.234"
time="${PERF_RESULTS[$runtime-$test_name]}"

# After (Bash 3.2+ compatible)
PERF_RESULTS=""
set_result PERF_RESULTS "jstime-bench-arithmetic" "1.234"
time=$(get_result PERF_RESULTS "$runtime-$test_name")
```

The helper functions use `eval` safely with script-controlled inputs (runtime names, test names, numeric timing values).

## Visual Example

The performance comparison now uses color coding:

![Benchmark Results](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/2d474333-4390-48a4-9ae7-9bda39d43348)

- 🟢 **Green** (★) = Fastest runtime
- 🔴 **Red** = Slowest runtime
- 🟡 **Yellow** = Middle performers
